title: Finite cohomology commutes with Noetherian derived completion
statement:
Let $A$ be a commutative Noetherian ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], let $I\subseteq A$ be any ideal, and let $L\in D(A)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] have finitely generated cohomology modules $H^q(L)$ for every $q\in\mathbf Z$ [def-weil-finitely-generated-module]. Define
$$F_I(L)=R\varprojlim_{n\geq1}(L\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}A/I^n),$$
using a K-flat resolution [def-pc-kflat-complex] for the derived tensors and the functorial mapping fibre of $1-\mathrm{shift}$ on termwise products of a strict complex-level tower for $R\varprojlim$ [def-weil-derived-limit]. Let $\eta_L:L\to F_I(L)$ be the natural map induced by the quotient maps $A\to A/I^n$. Then for every integer $q$ there is a natural isomorphism
$$H^q(F_I(L))\cong\varprojlim_{n\geq1}H^q(L)/I^nH^q(L),$$
under which $H^q(\eta_L)$ is the ordinary completion map $x\mapsto(x\bmod I^nH^q(L))_n$. In particular, for any finitely generated $A$-module $N$, there is a natural isomorphism $F_I(N[0])\cong(\varprojlim_nN/I^nN)[0]$ carrying $\eta_{N[0]}$ to that canonical completion map in degree zero.

source.place: Tag 0A06 (lemma-derived-completion-pseudo-coherent), statement and finite-free-resolution proof, including the induced cohomology maps; Tag 0922 (proposition-noetherian-naive-completion-is-completion) identifies this completion with the derived quotient-tower model and its unit.

proof.text: First let $K\in D(A)$ have finite cohomology and $H^i(K)=0$ for $i>m$. By [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-pseudocoherent-cohomology-criterion], $K$ is pseudo-coherent. Apply [lem-pc-pseudo-coherent-bounded-finite-free-model] with $b=m$ to obtain $P^\bullet\to K$, a quasi-isomorphism with each $P^j$ finite free and $P^j=0$ for $j>m$. In particular this applies to $K=\tau_{\leq m}L$: good truncation [def-kun-truncations] preserves $H^j(L)$ for $j\leq m$ and kills the remaining cohomology.

source.place: Tag 0A06 (lemma-derived-completion-pseudo-coherent), first two proof sentences; Tags 066E and 064U

proof.text: Finite free modules are flat: tensoring with $A^{\oplus t}$ is taking $t$ copies, so it preserves exact sequences. Thus [lem-pc-module-bounded-flat-kflat] makes $P^\bullet$ K-flat, and its strict tower $T_n=P^\bullet/I^nP^\bullet$ represents all the derived quotients and their quotient transitions. The maps $T_{n+1}^j\to T_n^j$ are surjective. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-surjective-module-complex-tower-limit] with the constant ring tower $A_n=A$, so its limit ring is $A$. It computes the limit as the complex $\widehat P^j=\lim_nP^j/I^nP^j$. The comparison to the stipulated mapping fibre is the chain map sending a compatible family to that family in the unshifted product coordinate and zero in the other coordinate. Degreewise $1-s$ is surjective: given $(y_n)$ choose $x_1=0$ and recursively lift $x_n-y_n$ to $x_{n+1}$. Its kernel is precisely the compatible families. Hence this inclusion of the kernel into its mapping fibre is a quasi-isomorphism. We therefore obtain $F_I(K)\simeq\widehat P^\bullet$ compatibly with the quotient projections and with the map from $P^\bullet$.

source.place: Tag 0A06, quotient tower and termwise inverse limit; Tag 091D (lemma-compute-Rlim-modules), clauses (3),(5)

proof.text:
Put $Z^q=\ker(d:P^q\to P^{q+1})$ and $B^q=\operatorname{im}(d:P^{q-1}\to P^q)$. Both are finite by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-submodule-finite]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-completion-exact-finite-modules] to
$$0\to Z^q\to P^q\to B^{q+1}\to0,\qquad 0\to B^q\to Z^q\to H^q(P)\to0.$$
All their terms are finite. Completion of $B^{q+1}\hookrightarrow P^{q+1}$ is injective, by applying the same node to its quotient sequence (the quotient is finite because it is a quotient of $P^{q+1}$). Since the completed differential factors as the completed surjection onto $B^{q+1}$ followed by that injection, its kernel is $\widehat Z^q$. Applying this in degree $q-1$, its image is $\widehat B^q\subseteq\widehat Z^q$. The second completed sequence therefore gives
$$H^q(\widehat P^\bullet)=\widehat Z^q/\widehat B^q\cong\widehat{H^q(P)}=\varprojlim_nH^q(K)/I^nH^q(K).$$
This calculation needs only the three adjacent terms, so there is no lower boundedness assumption on $P^\bullet$.

source.place: Tag 0A06, exactness of completion on finite modules; Algebra Tag 00MB (lemma-completion-flat), clause (2)

proof.text: The comparison just constructed is natural, including the unit. Indeed, for a chain map $u:P\to P'$ the maps on $Z^q$, $B^q$ and $H^q$ commute with the inclusions and quotient maps in step 3. Completion applies to a map componentwise on the residue classes, so the two completed exact sequences and their quotient identifications commute with $u$. A chain homotopy also completes termwise, preserving $u-v=dh+hd$. By [lem-pc-ring-derived-map-representative], any derived morphism between these bounded-above free models is represented by a chain map, uniquely up to homotopy; thus these identifications are independent of models and natural for morphisms of bounded-above finite-cohomology objects. For a cycle $z\in Z^q$, the map $P\to\widehat P$ sends $z$ to $(z\bmod I^nP^q)_n$. In the quotient $\widehat Z^q/\widehat B^q$ its image is the image of $z$ under $Z^q\to\widehat Z^q\to\widehat{H^q(P)}$, which is $([z]\bmod I^nH^q(P))_n$. This proves precisely the claimed description of $H^q(\eta_K)$ for bounded-above $K$.

source.place: Tag 0A06, natural cycle-and-boundary identification in the finite-free-resolution proof; explicit quotient-unit tracking

proof.text: Now allow $L$ to be unbounded. By [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], choose finitely many generators $a_1,\ldots,a_r$ of $I$. Fix $q$ and choose $m\geq q+r$. The natural map $i_m:\tau_{\leq m}L\to L$ is an isomorphism on $H^i$ for $i<m+1$ and injective on $H^{m+1}$, since its source in that degree is zero [def-kun-truncations]. Apply [lem-per-noetherian-completion-low-degree-bound] with $b=m+1$. It gives an isomorphism $H^q(F_I(i_m))$, since $q<m+1-r$. Compose its inverse with the isomorphism of steps 1--4 for $\tau_{\leq m}L$ and the canonical identification $H^q(\tau_{\leq m}L)=H^q(L)$. This gives the asserted isomorphism. Increasing $m$ does not change it: the inclusion between upper truncations and $i_m$ compose to the later $i_{m'}$, and step 4 gives the corresponding commuting square. For a morphism $L\to L'$, take the same $m$ on both sides and apply this square to the functorial truncation map; this proves naturality. Naturality of the quotient units gives $F_I(i_m)\eta_{\tau_{\leq m}L}=\eta_Li_m$, so the unit description from step 4 passes to $L$ as well.

source.place: Tag 0A06, final proof sentence; Tag 0AAJ (lemma-derived-completion-finite-cohomological-dimension), clause (2), via Tag 0922

proof.text:
Finally put $L=N[0]$. Its only nonzero cohomology is the finite module $N$ in degree zero. The result already proved makes $F_I(N[0])$ have zero cohomology in every other degree and degree-zero cohomology $\widehat N=\lim_nN/I^nN$. The good-truncation zigzag
$$F_I(N[0])\longleftarrow\tau_{\leq0}F_I(N[0])\longrightarrow H^0(F_I(N[0]))[0]$$
consists of quasi-isomorphisms: on cohomology both maps are the identity in degree zero and between zero modules otherwise [def-kun-truncations]. It gives the natural derived isomorphism with $\widehat N[0]$. The same zigzag for the source $N[0]$ shows that the induced map is $H^0(\eta_{N[0]})[0]$, hence the ordinary completion map found in steps 4--5.
